Hi Susan — thanks for sending this over and for the positive feedback on the demo. We're compiling a line-by-line response and routing the IP/indemnity sections through our contracts team. For initial clarity:

- IP: Redwood's position is that customer data (prompts, uploaded content) remains customer property; Redwood provides a limited license to operate the model for inference. We do not claim ownership over customer prompts or customer-provided content. We will propose language that explicitly states customer retains ownership of their inputs and outputs derived solely from those inputs.

- Indemnity: We generally provide indemnity for claims that Redwood materially breaches its obligations or for infringements attributable to Redwood-supplied software (not third-party OSS). We typically exclude claims arising from customer modifications, combined use with third-party code outside our supported integrations, or data provided by the customer.

- Liability cap: Our standard commercial cap is the greater of (a) fees paid in the prior 12 months or (b) $5,000,000. We can discuss upward adjustments for enterprise commitments.

- Data residency / PHI: We can commit to US-only processing and storage for regulated workloads on Private deployments (VPC/on-prem). For hosted API, we offer region pinning in certain cloud regions and SOC 2 attestation. We will call out audit log export capabilities and retention windows in the attached spreadsheet.

I've attached a draft spreadsheet with our proposed clause-level answers: Redwood_MedTech_Contract_QA_v1.xlsx (attached).

Next steps: Marissa and Aditya from our contract/tech teams will review and propose final edits. Can we target 11/1 for a consolidated response to your legal team? Also: does MedTech require any specific export-control language for model weights/evaluation artifacts?

Thanks,

--
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-30 14:23 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedTech: Contract questionnaire — internal review notes

Tessa / Aditya / Laura — quick internal notes on the draft QA spreadsheet (inline edits saved in a copy):

1) IP: Change wording to "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data and Outputs derived solely from Customer Data"; add a short clause that Redwood retains rights in the model and any model improvements generated independent of specific customer data. This avoids surprise on model retraining language.

2) Indemnity: Propose reciprocal indemnity for IP claims (each party indemnifies for their own IP infringement). For third-party OSS, add language that Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to cure or replace and will not accept indemnity for OSS claims beyond our ability to control. Add a carveout for customer misuse (e.g., prompting to infringe).

3) Liability cap: Customer asked for $10M or fees. We propose counter: greater of fees paid in prior 12 months or $7,500,000. If MedTech will commit to a 12–24 month committed spend (Order Form), we can agree to $10M. Note: mark as negotiation point on the deal profile.

4) Data residency / PHI: For hosted API we cannot guarantee strict PHI compliance unless on a Private deployment (VPC + dedicated capacity); propose an appendix that lists deployment options + costs. Include retention windows (audit logs 90 days by default, extended retention as paid add-on).

5) Order form: We can sign a mutually agreed order form; preferred approach is provide our standard order form with customer-specific fields filled and then accept customer's PO. If MedTech insists on their master order form, legal will redline.

I've attached the suggested final language file and flagged items that need commercial approval.

Attachments referenced: Redwood_MedTech_Contract_QA_InternalEdits.docx (internal use)

Marissa Cole
Senior Contracts Manager — Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: Redwood responses to MedTech contract questionnaire (attached)

Hi Susan (and MedTech legal/procurement),

Appended are our finalized, clause-level responses to the MedTech questionnaire. Summary of the key points below and the attached XLSX has the redlines inline as requested. We aimed to be pragmatic and left a small set of negotiation points (liability cap, deployment cost for Private PHI handling).

Summary of commitments:
- IP: Customer retains ownership of prompts and customer-provided content. Redwood retains rights to the model and general improvements not derived from Customer Data. Suggested clause text is in the spreadsheet.
- Indemnity: Reciprocal IP indemnity by default. Redwood will indemnify for claims arising from Redwood-supplied software/hardware breaches of license. OSS claims: Redwood will use reasonable efforts to remediate; cannot provide unlimited OSS indemnity.
- Liability cap: Proposed commercial position — greater of fees paid in prior 12 months or $7,500,000. If MedTech signs the attached OrderForm with a minimum committed spend (see OrderForm_MED-2026-0421.pdf), Redwood will agree to a $10,000,000 cap.
- Data residency & PHI: For PHI or regulated workloads we require Private deployment (VPC/dedicated capacity). Hosted API can be region-pinned for non-PHI workloads and includes SOC2 compliance evidence. Audit logs can be exported; default retention 90 days, extended retention available as a paid add-on.
- Order form: Attached is our populated OrderForm (OrderForm_MED-2026-0421.pdf). We can sign via DocuSign once mutual redlines are resolved.

Attachments: Redwood_MedTech_Contract_QA_Final.xlsx (final clause-by-clause responses), OrderForm_MED-2026-0421.pdf (pre-populated order form)

DocuSign link (pre-populated): https://www.docusign.com/packets/xyz-OrderForm-MED-2026-0421
Drive folder with supporting SOC2 and audit log screenshots: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-Redwood-MedTech-RFP

Next steps:
1) Please confirm if MedTech can accept the OrderForm with the $10M cap conditional on the committed spend. If yes, we will route to DocuSign by EOD 11/3.
2) If MedTech requires the $10M unconditionally, we will need commercial approval and may request an upfront payment schedule or additional term commitment.

Happy to set a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the spreadsheet — propose 10:30am PT.

Best regards,

Tessa Morgan
